question: how many ng employees in BCG USA in 2026?

target.what: Number of employees (headcount, 'ng' interpreted as number of) working at Boston Consulting Group (BCG) in the United States, as a stock at a point in 2026
target.publisher: No official publisher; BCG does not publicly disclose US headcount. Best available proxies: BCG global headcount disclosures, consulting-industry headcount surveys (e.g., Management Consulted, Consulting.ca, Vault), LinkedIn/company size data, and US office-level estimates
target.caveats: Ambiguity: 'ng' likely means 'number of'. Interpretation chosen: total US headcount (all staff levels, including consultants, support, and business services) at BCG's US offices, as a stock during 2026. Alternatives: (a) only client-facing consultants/consulting staff, excluding support; (b) only MB

candidates.hypothesis: BCG occasionally discloses global employee counts (e.g., 'over 25,000 employees worldwide'). US headcount = global headcount × US share. US share can be estimated from revenue share (US is roughly 35-45% of BCG global revenue) adjusted for revenue-per-employee differences between US and other regions.
candidates.data_to_find: BCG global employee headcount for 2024-2026 from BCG.com, press releases, or annual reviews; BCG global revenue and US revenue share from industry rankings (e.g., Kennedy, Source Global Research, Consultancy.org). Minimum: one global headcount figure and one US revenue share estimate.
search_hints: BCG US revenue share consulting market

candidates.hypothesis: Third-party trackers (Management Consulted, Consultancy.org, Vault, Glassdoor, LinkedIn) publish BCG employee counts, often split by office or country. These can be summed across US offices (Boston, NYC, Chicago, SF, DC, Dallas, etc.) to approximate US headcount.
candidates.data_to_find: BCG US office-level employee counts or US-total headcount from Management Consulted, Consultancy.org firm profiles, LinkedIn 'company size' for BCG US, or Glassdoor. Minimum: one US-total or office-sum figure for 2024-2026.

candidates.hypothesis: BCG's US headcount can be benchmarked against peers with disclosed US or global counts. If McKinsey US headcount and BCG/McKinsey global ratio are known, BCG US ≈ McKinsey US × (BCG global / McKinsey global) × adjustment for US share differences.
candidates.data_to_find: McKinsey US headcount and global headcount; Bain US/global headcount; BCG global headcount. Minimum: peer US and global counts plus BCG global count.

candidates.hypothesis: US headcount = prior-year US headcount + US hires − US attrition. US hires can be estimated from MBA/undergrad recruiting volumes (BCG hires X consultants per year) and experienced-hire postings; attrition from consulting industry turnover rates (~15-20%).

assumptions.name: US share of BCG global headcount

by_construction: Only URLs leave the searcher (code regex); extractor, judge and final prompts never contain search result titles, snippets or the searcher's text. This holds by construction and is not measured.
residual_risks: The searcher sees post-cutoff search results and chooses which URLs are fetched, so page selection can be conditioned on the answer; only the URLs leave the searcher, and in backtests every fetched page is a snapshot dated <= as_of.
Live pages are used only when as_of is today; in backtests every page is an archived snapshot dated <= as_of.
The leak sentinel only catches registered official values in common formats, not paraphrased or derived numbers.
The model's own training data (knowledge cutoff unpublished) can include history before as_of; it cannot include the target if the target was published after the model's release.
Wayback snapshots are captured by a third party; a snapshot date <= as_of proves the content existed by then.
Assumption values are proposed by the judge model from its own knowledge, which can include the target's history before as_of; code checks their form, not where the number came from.

The magnitude gate (v2.15d) asks the model once, without retrieval, for a rough estimate; whether the evidence-based estimate is more than 2x above or below it can carry the model's memory of the target into one repair. The rough number itself never enters a computation or a prompt; the estimate before that repair is kept in judge_rounds[-1].magnitude_checks[0]. The gate is off in the own-history ablation.
